ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, as amended; Executive Regulations of the Anti-Money Laundering Law (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 64 of 2003, as amended); Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) AML/CFT binding instructions for banks and non-bank financial institutions; Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) customer due diligence rules; Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended (including Law No. 4 of 2009 and Law No. 176 of 2018) requiring beneficial ownership identification for company registration; Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations establishing GAFI registration procedures

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national passport authority of the UBO/shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Egypt is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; document must be legalized by the competent Egyptian Consulate, preceded by notarization and foreign ministry authentication in the source country)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Principals / corporate shareholders before an Egyptian Notary Public or competent foreign notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (when executed abroad); if executed in Egypt, notarization before the Egyptian Notary Public and translation into Arabic

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory automated and manual screening before onboarding: (i) in-house AML team and external counsel will screen each UBO, director, manager, and corporate shareholder maintaining a direct or indirect 25%+ interest against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN lists, EU consolidated sanctions list, UK HM Treasury sanctions list, and Egyptian domestic terrorism and money-laundering lists issued under Law No. 80 of 2002; (ii) open-source adverse media and enforcement database review; (iii) politically exposed person (PEP) determination using a 12-month look-back and, if positive, enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval; (iv) source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification for all non-arm's-length capital contributions; (v) perpetual periodic re-screening every 90 days during the incorporation process and annually thereafter.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - 'Invest in Egypt' One-Stop Shop / Egyptian Companies Registry Online Platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in the Arabic language and follow Arabic naming conventions. A Latin-script parallel name may be added only if it is a phonetic transliteration or direct translation of the Arabic name. All names with foreign elements are examined to prevent duplication, misleading similarity, and violation of public policy. The name must end with the liability suffix 'Limited Liability Company' or 'LLC' in accordance with Companies Law No. 159 of 1981.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the GAFI Name Clearance Committee rejects the proposed Arabic/Latin name, the applicant or its authorized legal representative may, within 30 days from the rejection notice, submit a written administrative appeal to GAFI's Internal Grievance and Name Adjudication Committee stating the grounds of objection and demonstrating non-conflict with existing registrations and public policy. The committee must issue a reasoned decision within 30 days after receipt. If the administrative appeal fails, the applicant may file a judicial challenge before the Cassation Court / Administrative Court in the manner prescribed by the State Council Law, within 60 days from notification of the final administrative refusal. During the entire appeal process, the original name reservation may be extended for consecutive 30-day windows subject to payment of the applicable renewal tariff.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible. Under Egyptian Companies Law and GAFI practice, an LLC must maintain a physical, substantive registered office within Egypt that is not a bare virtual address. The lease or ownership evidence of the office must be submitted to the Commercial Registry, and the address must be capable of receiving official documents and regulatory visits. A 'virtual office' provider offering only a mailing address is not acceptable for this ISIC 7020 consultancy activity unless it provides a dedicated physical serviced office with a located manager and documented business operation; however, this is a high-risk practice and generally discouraged.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspections: 35% during the first 12 months of operation for a professional consultancy involved in cross-border tax structuring, given that GAFI, the Egyptian Tax Authority, and the Financial Regulatory Authority conduct routine substance-verification visits on knowledge-intensive services to confirm the registered office, personnel, records, and actual management presence.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, as amended (Articles 102-130 governing Limited Liability Companies); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations; Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976; Unified Tax Procedure Law No. 206 of 2020.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - One-Stop Shop (OSS), Commercial Registry and Investment Licensing Directorate, Governorate of Cairo.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Memorandum of Association (Aqd El-Taasis) and Articles of Association (El-Nizam El-Dakhili), GAFI incorporation application form, and resulting Commercial Registration Certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an Egyptian LLC. The founders fix the nominal capital, which must be divided into equal quotas. The entire cash portion of the capital must be deposited before registration into a temporary corporate bank account in Egypt; the bank issues a capital deposit certificate. Full cash payment is mandatory at incorporation. In-kind contributions must be independently valued and fully delivered. The deposit is released to the company after issuance of the Commercial Registration Certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription of the Company's quota capital, in the amount and allocation set forth in the Memorandum of Association, is hereby confirmed and allotted to the founding members named in the Shareholders' Register. RESOLVED, that the premises situated at [registered address], Governorate of Cairo, Arab Republic of Egypt, are adopted as the Company's registered office, and the General Manager is authorized to file the address with GAFI and the Commercial Registry. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed General Manager and [Name] is appointed Financial Compliance Officer, each authorized to open bank accounts, execute incorporation filings, and complete tax, social insurance, and Civil Defense registrations on behalf of the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Availability Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (OSS) / Commercial Registry, Governorate of Cairo
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File three alternative company names (in Arabic or Latin script) via the GAFI e-portal or at the OSS counter. Pay the name reservation fee and obtain the official name availability certificate. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity and must comply with Public Law naming restrictions.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation application form
Copy of founders' passports or national ID cards
Board resolution or authorization of any corporate founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as identical or confusingly similar, refile immediately with alternative names; an administrative review may be filed with the GAFI Legal Department within 30 days under the Investment Law Executive Regulations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office (Shahr El-Aqari), Governorate of Cairo
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the MOA and AOA in Arabic, including the company name, quota capital allocation, registered office, management structure, and business purpose (ISIC 7020 - tax structuring and transfer pricing advisory). All founders or their duly appointed attorneys holding notarized and legally translated powers of attorney must personally appear before the Notary Public to sign and attest the documents.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association (Arabic)
Passport copies of all founders and managers
Notarized, translated, and legalized power of attorney for any foreign founder
Company name reservation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies omissions, amend and resubmit the draft; if a foreign power of attorney lacks apostille or consular legalization, complete legalization at the Egyptian consulate in the country of issuance and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Temporary Bank Account and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank operating in Egypt (e.g., NBE, Banque Misr, or CIB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate account in the proposed company name using the notarized MOA/AOA. Deposit the full cash capital in EGP or a convertible foreign currency. The bank performs Central Bank of Egypt KYC/AML due diligence and issues a capital deposit certificate addressed to GAFI.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Company name reservation certificate
KYC and source-of-funds declarations for founders and managers
Passport copies of signatories and beneficial owners
AML screening forms per Central Bank of Egypt regulations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence, provide bank statements and wealth origin declarations; if the bank declines, deposit the capital with another licensed Egyptian bank and obtain the required certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (OSS), Cairo headquarters or governorate branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation file through GAFI OSS, including the notarized MOA/AOA, capital deposit certificate, notarized lease of the registered office, and completed GAFI application form. The OSS coordinates simultaneous issuance of the tax card, social insurance registration, and commercial registry entry in a single transaction. Pay statutory incorporation fees, publication fees, and stamp duties.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation application form
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Bank capital deposit certificate
Notarized office lease contract and building ownership consent
Police clearance / criminal record extracts for managers
Economic substance declaration and ultimate beneficial ownership statement
Receipts for payment of government fees (approx. USD 250 all-in)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the OSS issues a query or request for correction, remedy the filing by submitting corrected documents within 15 working days; any refusal may be appealed to the GAFI Central Administration for Investment Affairs within 60 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration and Official Gazette Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI OSS / Commercial Registry Authorities; Official Gazette (Al-Waqa'i Al-Masriya)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon OSS approval, receive the Certificate of Commercial Registration (incorporation certificate) containing the commercial registry number and legal entity identifier. GAFI transmits the incorporation notice for publication in the Official Gazette and the Enterprise Record (Kayd Al-Monasha'at) as required by Commercial Registry Law No. 34 of 1976.
required_dossiers: Approved incorporation file from GAFI OSS
Payment receipt for official gazette publication and registry fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed, request expedited processing from GAFI media/registry department; if registry data contains errors, file an administrative correction application with the Commercial Registry within 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Tax Card Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Regional Tax Office of the company's registered address
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete taxpayer registration under the Unified Tax Procedure Law No. 206 of 2020. The GAFI OSS data interchange normally auto-populates ETA records; obtain the Tax Card (Bitaqa Dribiyya) and Tax Identification Number (TIN). Register for electronic invoicing (e-invoice) and electronic receipt (e-receipt) systems if the company exceeds the ETA monetary thresholds for corporate taxpayers.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration Certificate
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association
Office lease contract
Copy of legal representative's passport or national ID
Bank account confirmation certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax card application is queried, supply the requested supplementary financial or identity documents to the ETA taxpayer services window; if e-invoice registration is rejected, verify system API credentials and resubmit through the ETA technical support portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI), Governorate of Cairo branch; Ministry of Labor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit social insurance registration Form 1 and salary declaration Form 2 for all managers and employees within one month of incorporation. Obtain the social insurance registration number. Employers with 10 or more workers must also file internal labor regulations with the Ministry of Labor under Labor Law No. 12 of 2003.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration Certificate
Office lease contract
Passport or national ID copies of all employees and managers
Form 1 (employment and wage registration) and Form 2 (salary statements)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NOSI file is queried, correct payroll figures and resubmit within the 30-day cure period; contribution disputes may be appealed to the NOSI internal disputes committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Civil Defense Fire Safety Approval and Occupational Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Civil Defense Authority, General Administration of Civil Defense, Ministry of Interior - governorate unit; licensed engineering office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the office floor plan, fire extinguisher specification, smoke detector layout, and emergency exit details to the Civil Defense Department. A civil defense inspector visits the registered office and, upon satisfactory inspection, issues the Fire Safety Certificate. A licensed engineer endorses the structural load clearance for the office space. The municipal authority confirms occupancy compliance for the consultancy use.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration Certificate
Office lease contract
Approved floor plan and structural load endorsement by a licensed engineering office
Fire extinguisher and smoke detector maintenance contract or supply certificates
Electrical installation safety certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the inspection flags deficiencies, remedy the fire safety items within the stipulated notice period and request a re-inspection; any disproportionate requirement may be appealed to the Civil Defense Technical Committee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Investment Licensing Directorate, One-Stop Shop; non-manufacturing service activity, so the Industrial Development Authority (IDA) license is not applicable.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: GAFI Investment Business License for Professional Services - International Tax Structuring and Transfer Pricing Advisory (ISIC 7020), integrated with Commercial Registration, Tax Card, and Social Insurance Registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category (C) - Low Environmental Risk: office-based consultancy activity is exempt from a full EIA report under Law No. 4/1994, as amended; a self-assessment environmental registration with the EEAA is recommended where the office is located in a mixed-use commercial building.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater or VOC-emitting manufacturing; domestic sewage discharge into the public sewer must meet municipal bylaws and Law No. 48/1982 non-industrial discharge limits (typical domestic maxima: BOD5 60 mg/L, COD 80 mg/L, TSS 50 mg/L); e-waste such as toners and batteries must be delivered to EEAA-registered recyclers; indoor noise levels must remain within 55 dB(A) for commercial premises during operating hours.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Fire Safety Certificate issued after inspection of the registered office, covering fire extinguisher placement, emergency exits, smoke detection, and evacuation signage; structural load inspection endorsed by a licensed engineering office confirming adequate office floor loading; occupational health and workplace safety clearance under Labor Law No. 12 of 2003 covering ventilation, lighting, electrical installation safety, restrooms, and first-aid facilities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA); e-services portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; electronic invoice portal: https://invoicing.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon incorporation through the General Authority for Investment (GAFI), the Egyptian LLC must register with the ETA to obtain a tax card containing the income tax ID and, if VAT-registered, the VAT registration number. Registration is completed using the commercial registration certificate, constitutional documents, director and shareholder identification, lease or ownership evidence of the head office, and the signed ETA registration forms; non-resident shareholders are generally not required to obtain an Egyptian TIN solely by holding shares unless they create a permanent establishment in Egypt.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; an Egyptian LLC is an opaque resident entity subject to corporate income tax on worldwide income under Law No. 91 of 2005 and to VAT under Law No. 67 of 2016 irrespective of dividend distribution.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election is available in Egypt. The only relevant statutory election is the tax grouping election under Law No. 91 of 2005, whereby an Egyptian parent company holding at least 95% of the share capital and voting rights of an Egyptian subsidiary may elect grouped taxation. Hybrid mismatch elections, foreign entity classification elections, and most OECD-type entity classification elections are not recognized in Egyptian domestic tax law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover; mandatory registration also applies to a single taxable supply exceeding EGP 500,000, and registration is immediately effective once the threshold is met
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered taxpayers must use the ETA e-invoicing system through approved clearing centers; invoices must be submitted in real time via the ETA API in the prescribed JSON/XML format and receive ETA clearance with a unique UUID and QR code before being treated as valid tax invoices. E-invoice clearance is mandatory for all B2B and B2G transactions, and e-receipt clearance is phased in for B2C sales; invoices without ETA clearance are invalid for input VAT deduction and legal documentation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and services are zero-rated for VAT when: (i) goods are physically delivered to a non-resident and leave Egypt within the statutory period; or (ii) services are provided to a non-resident person who uses or consumes the services wholly outside Egypt, including cross-border tax and transfer-pricing consultancy in respect of non-Egyptian entities. The exporter must possess contemporaneous evidence showing the export nature of the transaction, receipt of foreign currency in an Egyptian bank account, and consistency between the reported supply and the actual services or goods delivered.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (for goods, with ACI number in the Egyptian customs single-window)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (for physical exports)
Inward Remittance Certificate confirming receipt of convertible foreign currency
Commercial invoice or service agreement clearly identifying the non-resident recipient and the offshore nature of the services
ETA-cleared e-invoice with QR code evidencing zero-rated supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Unsubstantiated or fraudulent export zero-rating claims are subject to ETA reassessment at the 14% standard VAT rate, late-payment surcharges, statutory daily penalties, cancellation of the export certificate, and retrospective clawback of any refunded VAT. The ETA audits export documentation and foreign-exchange repatriation records; in cases of deliberate false documentation, criminal prosecution and fines are available under the Egyptian VAT Law and banking regulations, including restitution of the tax amount plus penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE); the CBE is the sole exchange-control authority and, through the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU), the national financial intelligence unit. The General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) also administers FDI-related registration and investment-file compliance for the LLC under Investment Law No. 72 of 2017.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations, ensuring current-account convertibility: ISIC 7020 consultancy fees, royalties, and management charges earned by EG_LLC may be invoiced, converted, and remitted to non-resident parties without exchange-control prohibition once the underlying service is documented and any applicable Egyptian tax is settled or exempted. Since the 6 March 2024 FX reform, the EGP is managed as a flexible currency priced by CBE-authorized banks on a daily interbank basis; no mandatory conversion or surrender ratio applies to current-account exports. The capital account remains regulated: inbound equity, shareholder loans, capital repatriation, liquidation balances, and profit remittances require documentary verification through a CBE-authorized bank, filing on the CBE integrated transfer platform, and reference to the GAFI investment file where applicable. Profit-remittance hurdles are procedural rather than prohibitive: audited Egyptian financial statements, tax clearance from the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) or a valid exemption certificate, correct beneficiary ownership declaration, sanctions screening by the remitting bank, and, for dividends, payment of the 5% or 10% dividend withholding tax as applicable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE Circular No. 12 of 2019 as amended by later circulars and the 2024 liberalization package, service-export proceeds for ISIC 7020 consulting contracts must be repatriated to a CBE-authorized Egyptian bank within 90 days from the invoice due date; a bank-approved extension to 120 days may be granted for contracts with inherently long settlement terms. The proceeds must be credited in the original hard currency to a designated Egyptian foreign-currency account and declared on the CBE integrated transfer reporting system. There is currently no mandatory conversion ratio; the exporter may retain 100% of proceeds in USD or EUR and convert to EGP at the prevailing interbank rate at its own election. The former 50% mandatory surrender that applied to selected goods-export categories before 2024 is not applicable to professional services provided the LLC maintains an executed client agreement, a milestone-dated invoice, and a matching inward SWIFT credit to the compliance account. Late repatriation disables access to the LLC's hedging lines, triggers automatic debit of proceeds toward credit facilities, elevates EMLCU reporting, and may block future CBE approvals for foreign-currency accounts or trade finance.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account in EGP and Operational Foreign-Currency Account in USD/EUR
Capital Escrow Account in EGP and Operational Current Account
Operational Multicurrency Current Account with Trade and LC Desk
Operational Multicurrency Account with International Connectivity
Operational Foreign-Currency Account for Retained Export Proceeds

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW. Wise, Revolut Business, Payoneer, Triple, and other foreign digital EMI platforms are not licensed by the CBE and may not provide CBE-supervised accounts to Egyptian corporates. An Egyptian LLC is prohibited under Article 233 of Law No. 194 of 2020 from maintaining offshore operational accounts without a prior, purpose-limited CBE authorization. Foreign EMIs may therefore be used only as peripheral payout-collection channels for low-value, non-resident client fees, with funds swept monthly into the onshore CBE-authorized compliance account. Routing equity injections, intercompany balances, or profit distributions through an unlicensed EMI is a definitive anti-money-laundering red flag, invalidates tax-clearance proof for remittances, and exposes the LLC's signatories to criminal exposure under Egypt's AML Law No. 80 of 2002. Onshore Egyptian fintech rails such as Fawry, Telr, and bank e-wallets are acceptable only for EGP-denominated local collections and cannot substitute for cross-border SWIFT settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for at least one legal representative of the LLC during the corporate account-opening KYC interview at a branch of the chosen CBE-authorized bank; remote account opening is effectively unavailable for a newly incorporated LLC in the Standard-Risk tier under ISIC 7020. A non-resident shareholder-manager who cannot travel may be substituted by an Egyptian resident attorney holding a notarized, Arabic-translated, and consular-legalized power of attorney; that attorney must appear physically with the original corporate kit. The bank will also require personal appearance or a verifiable liveness-checked video call for ultimate beneficial owners, production of the commercial registry extract, tax card, board resolution naming signatories, passport copies, proof of address, and a sanctions/PEP declaration. Physical attendance of the ultimate owner remains the safest route, particularly while EMLCU and CBE post-grey-list due-diligence standards remain elevated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Concentration of shareholding through Cyprus or UAE intermediate holding vehicles with an opaque beneficial-ownership layer, triggering PIP/PEP risk and CBE Circular due-diligence questions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: GAFI investment certificate and investment-file number; Arabic-notarized constitutional documents of the Egyptian LLC; full UBO chain analysis identifying every individual holding 25% or more; audited financial statements of intermediate holding companies for three years; share register and beneficial-owner register maintained under Law No. 80 of 2002; signed source-of-wealth declarations of ultimate owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds mismatch on the inbound capital injection, particularly remittances from third parties instead of the registered shareholder.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of bank statements for each investing shareholder; notarized share-subscription agreement; commercial registry extract; a documented explanation of any third-party remittance with recharacterization either as a registered shareholder loan under CBE inward-loan purpose coding or as a formal equity contribution filed with corporate authorities; tax receipts or wealth documents evidencing the origin of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border related-party fee flows at non-arm's-length pricing between EG_LLC, its offshore parent, and affiliated clients, creating an ETA transfer-pricing red flag and a possible trade- or services-based money-laundering indicator.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transfer-pricing policy documentation with local and master file prepared per Egypt's Transfer Pricing Guidelines under Decree No. 487 of 2023; signed intercompany agreement with fee formula and allocation keys; benchmarking study based on ISIC 7020 comparables; timesheet and deliverable-level service evidence; ETA tax returns including transfer-pricing schedules; an invoice-to-proceeds matching ledger.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Invoicing to opaque private clients or counterparties domiciled in high-sanctions-risk or intermediate jurisdictions, raising enhanced-due-diligence red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced CDD questionnaire completed by each counterparty; sanctions and PEP screening report covering UN, EU, OFAC, CBE, and other applicable consolidated lists with zero hits; counterparty beneficial-ownership declaration; signed statement of work and consulting agreement; ICC-aligned contract terms; auditable transaction trail maintained by the bank's compliance department.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Circularity from offshore EMI/wallet collection accounts where proceeds arrive from uncontrolled aggregator accounts rather than the direct client bank account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBE pre-approval for any offshore account or definitive evidence of closure; platform agreement with the EMI and settlement reports; six-month itemized collection ledger reconciled invoice by invoice; declaration that no funds originate from prohibited or unlicensed activity; legal opinion from Egyptian-seated counsel confirming compliance with Article 233 of Law No. 194 of 2020.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity must be remitted by SWIFT MT103 or MT202 from the shareholder's foreign bank to the EG_LLC escrow or operational account at a CBE-authorized Egyptian bank. The wire must carry the CBE inward-direct-investment classification for the acquisition of equity in an existing LLC and reference the GAFI investment-file number in SWIFT field 70, together with the corporate name, purpose, and invoice-equivalent capital-constitution reference. The beneficiary bank verifies the credentials against the commercial registry, tax card, and investment certificate, credits the designated exchange-control account, and converts FX to EGP at the interbank rate if the capital has been subscribed in EGP; otherwise it holds the hard currency in a legacy capital account. The subscribed capital must remain unencumbered until the commercial-registry amendment and statutory publication in the Official Gazette are completed. A shareholder remittance that is not equity must be submitted under the CBE inward-loan purpose code so that principal and interest can be serviced abroad under the applicable debt/equity rules; failure to classify accurately may lead to recharacterization, denial of interest deductibility, and withholding exposure. Every inbound leg is reported by the receiving bank to the CBE integrated transfer platform, and EMG/EMLCU sanctions screening is executed before credit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for subcontractors and non-resident service providers must be executed by SWIFT MT103 from the CBE-authorized Egyptian bank using the appropriate CBE current-account services-import purpose code and supported by the signed agreement, itemized invoice, proof of performance, and ETA withholding-tax certificate or exemption. For physical-goods procurement or software licenses on behalf of advisory clients, the standard clearing rail is a sight documentary letter of credit governed by UCP600 and opened through the Egyptian bank's trade desk, usually with 100% cover or an approved working-capital limit. Profit distributions to non-resident shareholders are a distinct gate: the remitting bank must receive audited financial statements, the ETA tax-clearance certificate, evidence of payment of dividend withholding tax, and the board resolution authorizing distribution; the wire must include the CBE dividend-repatriation purpose code. All outward instructions require dual signatories consistent with the account mandate, are screened against UN/EU/OFAC/CBE sanctions lists, and are reported to EMLCU where statutory thresholds apply.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contracts with CBE-authorized banks against documented ISIC 7020 service-export receivable and import-payable flows, standard tenor up to 12 months
FX swap agreements between Egyptian banks or between the LLC and its bank for EGP/USD liquidity transformation and settlement-date matching
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps on CBE-approved external borrowings, subject to prior CBE notification and underlying-loan documentation
Natural hedging through retained USD/EUR multicurrency current and legacy accounts at Egyptian banks without separate derivative pre-clearance

Onshore FX options where the authorized bank obtains full underlying-exposure documentation and CBE issues facility-level clearance; exotic options and offshore NDFs for resident entities are not standard and require special CBE authorization, which is normally granted only to banks hedging their own books

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Article 23, Law 91/2005)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months of fiscal year-end; calendar-year entities must file by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a minimum fine of EGP 10,000 plus 2% monthly late-payment surcharge on tax due; continued non-filing may lead to enforcement collection and license suspension through the Commercial Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audited Financial Statements and Shareholder Approval Record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be approved by the general assembly within 3 months of year-end and submitted to GAFI within 30 days of approval; for calendar-year LLCs the effective deadline is 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing triggers a warning notice and administrative fine under Companies Law 159/1981; repeated default may result in GAFI-initiated strike-off and disqualification of managers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office (General Department of Commercial Registration) / GAFI One-Stop Shop
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 January following the registration anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Renewal after the due date incurs a late fee of EGP 1,000 per month; outstanding renewal for more than 90 days subjects the entity to administrative strike-off and loss of CG registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Declaration and Register Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Regulatory Authority (FRA) and GAFI Anti-Money Laundering Compliance Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: UBO register must be confirmed by the board each financial year and filed with GAFI by 31 January
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit a true UBO declaration is an AML offense carrying fines from EGP 50,000 to EGP 200,000; deliberate concealment may trigger personal criminal liability of directors and ultimate shareholder disqualification.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for all limited liability companies regardless of size; every LLC must appoint at least one registered auditor (Law 159/1981 Art. 176–178). No small-company exemption for audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS) — substantively converged with IFRS; banks and financial institutions apply IFRS as issued.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually in the first quarter of the fiscal year, the board must review, update, and confirm the register of beneficial owners held at the registered office. Any shareholding transfer or change in UBO must be notified to GAFI within 30 days; the annual confirmation is a consolidated filing combining register updates and sign-off by the managing director.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday applies to Egyptian limited liability companies engaged in management consultancy activities. The base headline corporate income tax rate is 22.5% under Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005. Preferential regimes are limited to free-zone entities, certain newly established SMEs on the Egyptian Exchange, and export-linked incentives. A foreign tax credit may be available under Egypt's unilateral rules or double taxation agreements for qualifying foreign-source income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Egyptian Corporate Income Tax Return — Form No. 10 (Model No. 10), filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal at https://www.eta.gov.eg
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within four months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year company, no later than 30 April of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer legal name, commercial registration number, tax card number, and address of the Egyptian LLC
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete using the Egyptian LLC registration data; non-resident shareholder names are not entered in this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year beginning and end dates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Egyptian statutory accounting period; do not substitute the non-resident parent's consolidated fiscal year unless an ETA-approved different accounting period exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit before tax as per the Egyptian statutory financial statements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile from IFRS/GAAP statements after any Egyptian GAAP adjustments; the non-resident head office must not unilaterally reallocate income without TP documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from management consultancy, tax structuring, and transfer pricing advisory services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all revenue attributable to the Egyptian permanent establishment; offshore invoicing of Egyptian-selling labor is taxable and must be disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses: salaries, rent, professional fees, depreciation, licenses, and related-party expenditures
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident service provider fees are deductible only if withholding tax at the applicable statutory or treaty rate has been deducted and remitted to the ETA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income, special deductions, and investment incentives
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No exemption is available for cross-border tax structuring fees unless an explicit free-zone or bilateral treaty provision applies; supporting TRC and license must be attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transactions, applicable transfer pricing method, and economic substance narrative
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident controlled transactions aggregating above the ETA threshold require Form TP-1/TP-2 disclosure; insufficient documentation invites upward tax adjustment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an administrative fine of EGP 500 to EGP 10,000 and a monthly delay surcharge of 2% on unpaid tax, capped at 30% of the tax due. Failure to file after notification or submission of false documents may trigger criminal prosecution, additional tax penalties, and the attachment or freezing of corporate bank accounts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident beneficiary seeking a reduced dividend withholding tax rate under an applicable double taxation agreement must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the home jurisdiction tax authority, provide it to the Egyptian paying LLC or the ETA before payment, and submit a DTA relief declaration with beneficial-ownership statements. The Egyptian withholding agent must retain proof of treaty eligibility and obtain ETA clearance where the treaty imposes procedural conditions. If treaty relief was not applied at source, a refund application may be made through the ETA within the statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 20% withholding tax on payments for intellectual property, know-how, patents, and technical services; treaty rates may reduce this to 10% or 0% depending on the counterparty's jurisdiction. Interest: statutory 10% withholding tax on debt interest paid to non-residents; most Egyptian DTAs reduce or maintain interest rates between 5% and 10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EGP 10,000,000 aggregate controlled transactions per fiscal year triggers mandatory transfer pricing disclosure and local file preparation
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) exist in Egypt, but Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005 incorporates antiavoidance principles, substance-over-form, and general anti-abuse rules. The ETA may disregard artificial structures, recharacterize transactions, deny treaty benefits, and impose penalties if the Egyptian LLC lacks substantive activity such as a physical office, qualified staff, margin-bearing functions, and actual decision-making in regard to consultancy and tax structuring services.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of cross-border consultancy revenue, fabricating expenses, using sham invoicing, or omitting taxable payments routed through foreign subsidiaries
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty equal to 150%–200% of the evaded tax; interest and delay surcharges at 2% per month up to 30%; criminal fine and imprisonment up to five years under Egyptian Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners who approve false filings are jointly and severally liable for evaded tax, surcharge, and penalties; the corporate veil may be pierced upon proof of fraud, resulting in seizure of personal assets, travel bans, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing an Egyptian LLC with no employees, office, business conduct, or economic activity while attributing revenue to it solely to obtain treaty benefits or shift profit from a related non-resident entity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA application of general anti-abuse rules to disregard the entity and reallocate income; denial of treaty relief; tax reassessment with 22.5% CIT, late-payment surcharges, and penalty up to 200% in aggravated cases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and shareholders who knowingly use a shell structure face joint liability for the entire tax deficiency, administrative fines, and criminal sanctions for tax evasion; travel bans and asset freezes are available under Egyptian execution law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the mandatory TP disclosure forms, failure to prepare local/master file above the EGP 10,000,000 threshold, or pricing intercompany management fees and IP royalties outside the arm's length range
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Upward TP adjustment, denial of deduction for unsubstantiated related-party charges, administrative penalty for non-disclosure, and monthly delay surcharge of 2% on the tax deficiency, capped at 30%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The tax director and managing directors who sign false TP declarations may be personally assessed for surcharges and penalties; criminal liability may attach when misstatements are fraudulent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the consultancy LLC to facilitate laundering of proceeds through legal fees, structured wire transfers, unnamed beneficial ownership, or tax arbitrage schemes with criminal counterparties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Egypt's Anti-Money Laundering Law No. 80 of 2002, penalties include imprisonment up to 15 years, fines up to EGP 1,000,000, confiscation of funds, and freezing of corporate accounts; financial institution de-risking may also occur.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior management, directors, and beneficial owners who knowingly or negligently facilitate money laundering are exposed to direct criminal prosecution, travel bans, asset seizure, and disqualification from serving as directors.
